hypothesis: The full-text transposition search recovers all known-key controls exactly and exceeds the matched complete-search shuffle null on QTXMA.
refuted_by: A known-key control is not recovered exactly, or the target maximum fails complete-search calibration.
notes: This is a bounded smoke experiment, not an exhaustive double-transposition exclusion.
Only order-sensitive n-grams are optimized: Phase 6 uses the bootstrap scorer and Phase 7 substitutes published 1941 counts. Monograms are excluded because transposition preserves them.
Candidate keys are selected by scoring each complete proposed plaintext. Any prefix or suffix statistics are descriptive only.
The target widths are a small first-pass set centered on short hand-cipher keys and do not include every historically possible rectangle.
A score-only candidate is not an accepted break without coherent plaintext, historical procedure, and independent reproduction.
The candidate suffix is descriptive only; no independent held-out claim is made from it.
